So: a strong session, and 4:27/km at 160 bpm sixteen kilometres deep is real evidence of fitness, but it was a long run with a tempo finish rather than the easy long run it reads as — and embedded quality on long runs isn't due until mid-August. days.entry: 4 x 1 mile off three minutes standing, exactly as prescribed, and executed about as well as this session can be. The watch pauses during the recoveries, so the three gaps in the recording — 211, 172 and 200 seconds — mark the reps precisely: four blocks of 366, 363, 362 and 356 seconds. Split each rep at 1000 m and both halves of the assignment show up cleanly. The 5K-pace legs came in at 4:02, 4:00, 4:00, 3:58 — metronomic, and deliberately 8-10 s/km slower than actual 5K pace, which is the discipline this session tests. The mile-pace legs went 3:42, 3:40, 3:36, 3:29: at mile pace, then progressively through it, closing the final 560 m at 3:29/km. Rep averages fell every time (3:55, 3:53, 3:52, 3:48) and the gear change widened every time (20, 20, 24, 29 s/km). That is a negative-split set most runners don't manage. HR climbing 174 to 180 to 183 to 184, with recovery depth shrinking from 62 beats to 44 across the rests, is simply the price of four hard miles — and a 62-beat drop inside three minutes on the first rest is a strong number. Two caveats, neither a criticism of the session: CTL 27 is a young base to be running mile-pace work on, and mile speed is not the limiter here — endurance is. The one loose end is the cooldown at 155 bpm in Z3, which should sit in Z1-Z2. This also firms up the 5K picture: 4 x 1 mile averaging 3:52 off short rest sits with the critical-speed model's 19:07 rather than December's 19:17 being the ceiling.
